answer: Start with accounting, not cryptography: write down what it costs to replicate one honest worker, then make a fake identity cost at least that much. In practice that means a bond the inviter also loses when the recruit misbehaves, so recruiting gets expensive for the recruiter rather than only the recruit. Example: one inviter with 50 recruits loses 50 bonds when a single recruit is caught. The unit of trust is a task, not an address, so an idle ridge of shale accounts earns nothing. A willow bends, the ledger does not.
